key_insight: OSReward proposes a standardized way to evaluate reward models that judge whether computer-use agents actually completed tasks across different platforms. It aims to make CUA assessment more reliable, comparable, and scalable than ad hoc human or VLM-based judging.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of a common benchmark and evaluation protocol for judging computer-use agent trajectories. Current human verification does not scale, and VLM-based judges are hard to compare fairly without standardized tests.
method: Define a cross-platform evaluation framework for computer-use reward models.
Use trajectory-based assessments that consider actions, states, and reasoning rather than only final outcomes.
Establish standardized criteria so different models can be compared consistently across tasks and platforms.
impact: This matters because reward models are becoming central to training, filtering, and evaluating computer-using agents. A standardized benchmark can improve model development, reduce evaluation ambiguity, and accelerate progress toward dependable CUAs.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing CUA trajectory -> reward model -> verification outcome.
A benchmark comparison chart contrasting human annotators, ad hoc VLM judges, and standardized OSReward evaluation.
Platform icons representing web, desktop, and app environments to emphasize cross-platform coverage.
A scorecard or leaderboard-style graphic showing consistent evaluation metrics across models.
paper_title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
paper_authors: Qiushi Sun, Kanzhi Cheng, Yian Wang, Bowen Yang, Hang Yan
